text:
maya: Heads up — saw a perf regression on Mixtral-7B today after the kernel selector change. FlashAttention was chosen but then immediately fell back to SDPA for many requests (head_dim=48). latency p50 jumped ~35% :eyes:

sam: ugh. can you paste the trace? is it fallback due to headdim not multiple of 16?

maya: paste from prod trace (redacted):
```
[2026-03-17T22:10:43Z] kernel_selector: picked=flash, compat=false -> fallback=sdpa
[2026-03-17T22:10:43Z] fallback_reason=unaligned_head_dim (head_dim=48, align=64)
[2026-03-17T22:10:43Z] kv_cache_miss: prefetched=false, path=hot
[2026-03-17T22:10:43Z] batch_size=1 -> ramped to 8 after kvcache rebuild
[2026-03-17T22:10:43Z] latency_ms=64 -> 87
```

li: confirmed - Mixtral's head dim 48 is common. our flash kernel requires multiple of 16 (or 8 on some arch) and tries a vectorized path. Triton layer returns compat=false.

rohan: why does fallback cause big latency jump? sdpa should be fast too.

maya: SDPA is fine but our batching heuristics + kvcache recovery are the amplifier. Sequence: flash chosen -> kernel compat check fails late -> we requeue onto SDPA worker pool -> request misses warm KV slots -> we do extra KV shuffles -> small batches -> GPU underutilized.

jess: can you quantify kvcache miss impact?

maya: quick numbers from the run: p50 token time flash-friendly path ~= 7ms, fallback path median token time ~= 11.5ms (+64%). kvcache miss adds ~2.5ms per token when it needs to rebuild prefixes.

sam: ok. immediate mitigation options?

li: short-term: change selector to verify compat before enqueue and prefer SDPA for known head dims (48, 56, etc). medium-term: add a specialized Flash kernel for head_dim%16==0? wait 48%16==0 so weird — problem is alignment to 64 in our compiled kernel on some GPUs. need architecture-specific rules.

rohan: we already have architecture profiles saved in kernel_profiles. Could we use a quick lookup table: (arch, head_dim) -> preferred_kernel? fast to implement and low risk.

maya: I ran a canary yesterday with that table for a subset of Mixtral traffic — removed the late fallback and stabilized p50. no change to accuracy.

jess: what about RoPE scaling? I remember a change in rope precompute that could affect kvcache index calculations. any link?

maya: good catch. we found an edge case where RoPE scaling code path did float->fp16 truncation which changes mask offsets for long sequences. that interacts badly with our prefix KV addressing, causing more cache misses for long chats. reproducible with seq_len>1024.

li: example repro command (uses load-test image):
```
./run_infer --model mixtral-7b --head-dim 48 --rope-scale 1.5 --seq-len 2048 --batch 1
```

sam: thanks. action plan?

rohan: 1) revert selector hotpath to pre-check compat for incoming tensor shapes (fast)
2) add (arch,head_dim,rope_flag) whitelist in kernel_profiles for immediate routing
3) instrument KV cache hits/misses per-request in the trace so we can alert on regressions
4) longer term: implement a Flash microkernel variant tolerant of head_dim mod 16==0 vs mod 8 tradeoffs.

maya: I've opened a canary rollout PR that implements (1) + (2). hooking perf alerts to trace metric kvcache_miss_rate. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123

infra-bot: deploy triggered for runtime/canary (shard=us-west-2, 5% traffic) by maya.

li: small note — for Triton-backed builds we also need to guard for cudnn/cuBLAS ABI differences; some GPUs return success for flash but underperform. I'll add a micro-benchmark on startup to tag node capabilities.

jess: should we also update Optimize recommendations to prefer quantization profiles that keep head dims aligned? i.e., when quantizing/merging heads, prefer multiples of 8?

maya: yes, add a check in the model onboarding flow to flag non-standard head dims and suggest layout transforms or split-head tricks. won't auto-change anything without explicit opt-in.

sam: timeline?

maya: PR in review now for canary. if canary looks clean over 24h we promote. li will add the node micro-bench next patch. rohan will open a follow-up for the microkernel design. jess will add onboarding note.

rohan: I'll sketch microkernel API - low risk compatibility wrapper so we can A/B test.

li: reminder — add a metric join between kernel_selector.fallback_count and kvcache.miss_rate so we can see correlation.

maya: thanks all. I'll post a short postmortem if canary confirms. for now tagging @sam @li for visibility. :thumbsup:
